material.PLASTIC.label: Plastic
material.PLASTIC.instruction.2: Small caps can stay on in most municipalities
material.PLASTIC.instruction.3: Look for the recycling symbol (PET 1, HDPE 2, PP 5)
material.PLASTIC.description: Recycling PET saves up to 80% of the energy needed to make new plastic.
material.PAPER.label: Paper & cardboard
material.PAPER.instruction.0: Paper must be dry — wet paper can't be recycled
material.PAPER.dont.1: Wet wipes and dirty paper towels
material.PAPER.description: One tonne of recycled paper saves ~17 trees and 26,000 litres of water.
material.GLASS.label: Glass
material.GLASS.instruction.1: Don't shatter containers — glass is collected whole
material.GLASS.description: Glass can be recycled infinitely with no loss of quality — 100% circular.
material.METAL.label: Metal
material.METAL.instruction.2: Use a magnet: if it sticks it's ferrous metal (scrap yard)
material.METAL.dont.1: Batteries and electronics in the bin
material.METAL.description: One recycled aluminium can saves ~95% of the energy of a new one — enough to power a TV for 3 hours.
material.ORGANIC.label: Organic waste
material.ORGANIC.instruction.0: Use compostable bags or empty contents directly
material.ORGANIC.instruction.1: If you have a yard or balcony, compost at home
material.ORGANIC.instruction.2: Organic waste in residual bins produces landfill methane
material.ORGANIC.dont.0: Large amounts of cooking oil (separate collection)
material.ORGANIC.description: Composted properly, organic waste becomes fertiliser, not methane — a gas 80× stronger than CO2.
material.E_WASTE.label: E-waste
material.E_WASTE.instruction.0: Never in the regular bin — it holds valuable metals and toxins
material.E_WASTE.instruction.1: Take it to municipal collection centres (map it locally)
material.E_WASTE.instruction.2: Large retailers must take it back when you buy a new one
material.E_WASTE.instruction.3: Wipe your personal data before handing it in
material.E_WASTE.description: One tonne of circuit boards holds more gold than a tonne of gold ore.
material.BATTERY.label: Batteries
material.BATTERY.instruction.0: Never in the bin — one battery can contaminate 600,000 litres of water
material.BATTERY.instruction.1: Drop them at supermarkets, pharmacies or schools
material.BATTERY.instruction.2: Tape the terminals so they can't short-circuit
material.BATTERY.dont.2: Power banks — e-waste or dedicated point
material.BATTERY.description: Battery recycling recovers zinc, nickel, cobalt and lithium — critical e-mobility resources.
material.TEXTILE.label: Textiles
material.TEXTILE.instruction.0: Wash and dry clothes before collection
material.TEXTILE.instruction.1: Seal them in bags at special containers
material.TEXTILE.instruction.2: Wearable items are donated; worn-out ones become fibre
material.TEXTILE.dont.0: Textiles contaminated with chemicals or paint
material.TEXTILE.dont.2: Mixed-fibre knitwear that's hard to separate
material.TEXTILE.description: Extending a garment's life by just 9 months cuts its carbon footprint by 20–30%.
material.HAZARDOUS.label: Hazardous waste
material.HAZARDOUS.instruction.0: Cooking oil: sealed bottles at dedicated drop-off points
material.HAZARDOUS.instruction.2: Paint, solvents, chemicals: hazardous waste centres
material.HAZARDOUS.dont.0: Never pour oil or chemicals down the drain
material.HAZARDOUS.dont.1: Never mix them with regular waste
material.HAZARDOUS.description: One litre of oil poured down the drain can pollute up to 1,000 litres of water.
material.OTHER.label: Residual / unknown
material.OTHER.instruction.0: If it looks recyclable but you're unsure, take a closer photo
material.OTHER.instruction.1: Check the Sortify guide for categories
material.OTHER.instruction.2: Reduce first, reuse second, recycle last
material.OTHER.dont.0: Don't overuse the residual bin — most items have a dedicated stream
material.OTHER.dont.1: Never dump bulky items without a pickup appointment
material.OTHER.description: When in doubt, residual is the safe option — but check the guide first.
